Hi all — quick internal note on counting rules and a proposed concession for the quote. High level: we try to keep metering consistent with how the runtime constructs the request/response. Below are the practical rules and the commercial language I propose we give Anna. 

Metering rules (runtime behavior):
- Request side: billable = user input tokens + system message tokens that are passed in the request header. If a customer shows a requirement that a fixed short system prompt (<= 8 tokens) is mandatory for product safety, we can offer to absorb N tokens per request as a credit under committed tiers (see concession).
- Tool-calls: if the runtime executes a tool that returns structured metadata (non-text) it is not billed. If the tool returns text that we append to the assistant response, we count that text as assistant output (single-line attribution) — regardless of the number of internal sub-queries the tool performed, we will bill the aggregated returned text once. If the tool streams back multiple chunks we aggregate the final text for billing when using per-request rounding.
- Streaming rounding: two modes exist: per-chunk rounding (default) and per-request rounding (budget-friendly). Per-request rounding sums raw token usage and rounds at the end; this reduces variance. For committed-volume customers we can enable per-request rounding for invoices.

Proposed concession language for procurement (short, copy-paste):
"Redwood will count system prompt tokens as billable by default. For the 12-month committed tier specified in Deal ID SH-2026-11-BASIC, Redwood will apply a monthly credit equivalent to 5 system prompt tokens per hosted API request to reduce month-to-month variance, subject to a maximum monthly cap equal to 10% of the committed monthly token volume. This concession applies only to system messages that are stable and under 32 tokens in length and does not extend to tool-generated text returned as part of model responses."

Notes: the concession keeps billing predictable and limits exposure. If Marissa signs off we can add the exact cap numbers and put it in the quote. Neha, flag any legal caveats.

— Rishi
Head of Finance, Redwood Inference
